item.title: ONGC weighs standalone, joint venture models for new greenfield refinery
item.description: The state-run oil major is evaluating standalone, subsidiary and foreign partnership models for its proposed refinery, with capacity, investment and location yet to be finalised ...
item.dc:creator: Shubhangi Mathur
item.content:encoded: State-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd (ONGC) is evaluating various models for its proposed greenfield refinery and petrochemical complex, including setting it up independently, through a subsidiary, or in partnership with foreign players, people familiar with the matter said. “The project is in the initial stage and we are deciding the working model. Other specifications, such as location and configuration of the refinery will be worked out later,” a senior company executive said. The proposed refinery is also likely to have a higher petrochemical intensity, in line with rising domestic demand, the official said. The detailed feasibility report (DFR) will assess the refinery’s petrochemical configuration and potential, the official added. Questions sent to ONGC remained unanswered. The proposed greenfield refinery project assumes significance for ONGC's larger diversification and integration plan. The details regarding capacity and investment requirement for the project will be firmed up once the DFR is ready. Indian oil companies are pursuing a mix of greenfield refinery projects and expansions of existing plants to raise the country’s overall refining capacity. Earlier this month, oil minister Hardeep Singh Puri said India’s refining capacity of 267 million tonnes per annum (mtpa) helped ensure fuel availability despite supply disruptions during the peak of the West Asia conflict. The country’s refining capacity is expected to rise to 320 mtpa by 2030, he added. Countries such as Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) have also shown interest in investing in upcoming Indian refinery projects, provided they see meaningful returns on their investments, said Puri. Meanwhile, state-run Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd (BPCL) is developing a 9 mtpa greenfield refinery-cum-petrochemical complex at Ramayapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, with final environmental clearance expected soon. Indian Oil Corporation Ltd (IOCL), along with its subsidiary Chennai Petroleum Corporation Ltd (CPCL), is setting up a 9- mtpa greenfield refinery in Nagapattinam, Tamil Nadu, with a focus on meeting the rising demand. In July, HPCL commissioned a 9 mtpa greenfield refinery-cum-petrochemical complex in Rajasthan. India currently has 5.33 million tonnes (mt) of SPR capacity across Visakhapatnam, Mangaluru and Padur, while another 6.5 mt planned under Phase II. ONGC received approval to develop a 1.75-mt strategic petroleum reserve at Mangaluru, Karnataka, as an extension of the existing SPR facility. The project, estimated to cost around ₹7,000 crore, will be developed and financed by ONGC. About half of the storage capacity is expected to be reserved for strategic use, while the company has sought government approval to commercially utilise the remaining capacity. ONGC has already acquired land for the project.

item.title: Nilekani panel explores last-minute question papers to prevent exam leaks
item.description: The task force is considering large question banks, AI-generated papers and wider computer-based testing to prevent leaks, with recommendations expected within three months of its formation ...
item.dc:creator: Auhona Mukherjee
item.content:encoded: The Centre’s task force on examination reforms is considering generating question papers at the last minute from a large question bank to prevent leaks. The panel is expected to submit its recommendations within three months of its formation on July 28, Nandan Nilekani, who heads the high-powered task force, said on Tuesday. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, Nilekani said the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test (Undergraduate), or Neet (UG), paper leak had raised questions about the need for conventional question papers, given the financial incentive to obtain and sell them in advance. “So I think the question becomes, why do we need to have something called a question paper? Because the moment you have a question paper, that creates an economic incentive for that to be sold. So the way to do it is to really have a massive bank of questions. And only at the last minute, generate the question paper for that day,” he said. This approach would remove the financial incentive to obtain and sell question papers in advance, he added. Nilekani said artificial intelligence (AI) could also be used to generate question papers on the day of an examination to prevent leaks. The panel is also examining the expansion of computer-based testing, which would require a wider network of examination centres, he said. India currently has around 150,000 locations where candidates can take tests, and this network needs to expand, Nilekani observed. “We have 150,000 locations where a young boy or girl can take a test. That needs to be expanded. So I think these are all systemic issues which we will address in our committee,” he said. The committee would identify the root causes of examination-related problems and use technology to address systemic weaknesses, Nilekani said, adding that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was keen to implement its recommendations. Modi announced the formation of a high-powered task force led by the Infosys cofounder on July 26, following protests over the Neet (UG) 2026 paper leak and demands for accountability in the examination system. The Centre subsequently informed the Supreme Court that the panel would recommend reforms to strengthen the security and credibility of competitive examinations, particularly those conducted by the National Testing Agency. AI could help India improve literacy and numeracy among millions of people, Nilekani said. AI tools could also make information more accessible by allowing people to interact with computers in their preferred languages, he added. Nilekani dismissed concerns that AI would lead to widespread job losses in India’s information technology services sector, calling the argument “absolutely hogwash”. Companies would need greater support to fundamentally transform their operations using AI, creating more work for technology services firms, he said. “I think this is all disaster marketing to suit the interests of large capital. The fact of the matter is that the requirement for companies like Infosys or others is actually more than ever before because the transformation of enterprise is a very complex activity. And AI requires fundamentally reimagining the way you do business. And it’s a root and branch surgery that is required. And this, in fact, even more requires firms like ours to show companies how to go about making those transformations, how to reimagine the future,” he said. Nilekani said companies would need to transform their operations, reskill workers, and build new capabilities to adopt AI, adding that the technology’s capabilities were far ahead of its deployment. While AI coding agents would make coding more productive, he said, most of the work in technology projects extended beyond coding to include governance, change management, and business transformation. New jobs would emerge in understanding client requirements, coordinating teams, and ensuring AI systems did not hallucinate or behave unpredictably, he added. Small businesses could become a major source of job creation if AI improved their productivity and gave them better access to markets, capital, and information, Nilekani said. Millions of small enterprises could expand and hire more workers as a result, he added. India’s strength lay in applying AI at scale rather than competing solely to build models and computing infrastructure, Nilekani said, citing the country’s experience with digital public infrastructure such as Aadhaar and the Unified Payments Interface.

item.title: Trump says he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran at all
item.description: Trump says Moscow and Beijing have too much to lose by helping Tehran, amid reports of possible Russian targeting support and Chinese assistance during the Iran war ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / Trump says he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran at all

Trump says he does not believe China and Russia are helping Iran at all Trump says Moscow and Beijing have too much to lose by helping Tehran, amid reports of possible Russian targeting support and Chinese assistance during the Iran war

President Donald Trump (Photo:PTI)

Reuters Washington 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 13 2026 | 11:42 PM IST

Listen to This Article

President Donald Trump said late on Monday he did not believe that China and Russia were helping Iran "at all," adding that Moscow and Beijing had "too much to lose" if they enabled Tehran.   Trump said on Truth Social that he had seen comments from his critics and opponents that China and Russia were helping Iran.   "If they are, it's at a very low level, but I don't believe they are at all. They have too much to lose, and we would know about it, and know about it very fast," Trump wrote.   Trump said in July he trusted China and Russia not to help Tehran in the Iran war, but warned that if they did get involved, "it would be very bad for them."

The United States and Iran have been at war since February 28, when the US and Israel attacked Iran and Tehran responded with its own strikes on Israel and Gulf states that host US bases. US-Israeli strikes on Iran and Israeli attacks on Lebanon have since killed thousands and displaced millions. Also Read

China opposes India's move to name 28 strategic locations in Ladakh

Trump's diesel deal with Russia irks allies, unlikely to reduce prices

Trump's deal with Russia gives Putin a boost in economic war with Ukraine

Trump has previously described Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin as "neutral" during the Iran war.   Iranian drone attacks on CIA facilities in the Gulf have prompted US intelligence analysts to investigate whether Russia provided targeting information or advanced drone technology.   European foreign ministers pressed the case in a March meeting with US Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The Washington Post and The Wall Street Journal reported that month that Russia was providing Iran with targeting information.

Moscow and Beijing maintain close ties with Tehran. Russia has said the Iran war could lead to a nuclear arms race in West Asia. Beijing has condemned Washington's attacks on Tehran as a brazen violation of Iran's sovereignty.   Last month, Trump warned Xi against providing support to Iran when the Chinese leader visited Washington, and received assurances that China would not do so, the US ambassador to China said at the time.   The warning came amid reports that China had supplied Iran with shoulder-fired air-defence missile launchers and that Tehran had found ways to evade sanctions on its oil sales with Chinese help.

In September, Trump brushed aside a report that Iran acquired satellite images of a base in Jordan from Chinese entities before an attack that killed three US troops there in July.

item.title: Apple needs new iPhones and smart-home push to revive pricey stock
item.description: The iPhone maker is holding a smart-home products event on Tuesday featuring an Apple doorbell and Apple thermostat ...
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg
item.content:encoded: By Ryan Vlastelica Apple Inc. is rolling out a slew of new products and improved older ones this week, but investors are unsure if it will be enough to boost one of the most expensive stocks in the market that’s largely gone nowhere in months. The iPhone maker is holding a smart-home products event on Tuesday featuring an Apple doorbell and Apple thermostat, according to a Bloomberg News report. Later this month, the company is planning to launch a touchscreen MacBook and a new iPad mini. And on Friday, pre-orders begin for the new foldable iPhone Duo, which represents the biggest design change in the history of Apple’s most profitable device and carries a commensurately hefty price tag. The stakes are high for Apple shares, which soared to a record in late July amid reports about its push into the smart-home market and skepticism about heavy artificial intelligence spending that Apple has avoided. But the stock is basically flat in the months since. “For a company of this size, you need super-hit products to move the needle on growth,” said Peter Andersen, who helps oversee $5.5 billion as chief investment officer of Andersen Capital Management. “I’m just not sure anything we’re getting is exciting enough to lead to an inflection.”  The stock is up 25% this year, making Apple the top performer among the Magnificent Seven tech giants. It trades at more than 35 times earnings estimated over the next 12 months, right around its highest multiple since 2007 and well above its 10-year average of 24. Apple is among the 50 most expensive stocks in the S&P 500 Index, which is priced at 19 times forward earnings.  Some of that reflects Apple’s unique position within the AI trade, where it isn’t exposed to spending risk but is considered a key beneficiary of the technology’s development. And it shows investors’ high expectations for new Chief Executive Officer John Ternus and their hopes that he can generate growth by upgrading and expanding its lineup of devices. That’s a risk, however. The company has cut component orders for some iPhone models due to weaker-than-expected demand, according to a Bloomberg Intelligence report last week. Meanwhile, consumers are feeling pressured by stubborn inflation, and Apple has had to raise prices due to higher costs for components like memory chips.  “Apple executes its products flawlessly, but it’s hard to expect these will really take off,” said Andersen, who doesn’t own the stock, in part due to what he sees as the company’s lack of innovation. “Not only have there been major players in the home market for years, but Apple is launching these products into a market where consumers are under a lot of pressure.” What’s more, Apple’s growth rate is lagging its Big Tech peers, making its high stock market valuation stand out even more than it already does. The company’s fiscal year ended on Sept. 30, and it’s projected to post a 15% rise in annual revenue when it reports earnings in a few weeks. But that appears to be a near-peak, with the pace expected to slow to 10% in fiscal 2027 and 7.8% in fiscal 2028.  “Apple doesn’t look like a value stock or a growth stock,” Andersen said. “Given where the multiple is, it seems questionable to expect much additional stock upside from here.” Of course, Apple isn’t alone in its slowing growth. Overall tech sales are expected to experience a deceleration in the coming years, albeit off a much higher level. Revenue is projected to climb 37% for the S&P 500 information tech sector in 2026, and 29% in 2027, according to Bloomberg Intelligence. Whether Apple’s new products will alter the company’s earnings outlook remains to be seen. But Wall Street hasn’t been racing to adjust its projections. Analysts’ expectations for the company’s fiscal 2027 net income have dipped by 0.6% over the past three months, while their view for revenue has risen 0.7%.  “Apple’s product path seems promising, but I don’t think the first generation of new products will mean much for overall revenue,” said Lu Zhang, founder and managing partner of Fusion Fund, who owns the stock in her personal portfolio. “It remains to be seen whether we will see the kind of new use cases (for the foldable Duo) that will contribute to a broad upgrade cycle.” Nevertheless, Zhang remains positive on the stock. Apple could improve its AI offerings, she said, but it will continue to benefit from being a gateway for consumers to access the emerging technology. “All the AI companies are competing with each other, but whenever they launch a new model they need Apple as a key distribution channel, and that’s an area where it essentially has no competitor,” she said. “Even if Duo adoption isn’t high right out of the gate, so long as Apple continues to execute on its hardware, it will warrant a premiere multiple.” Tech Chart of the Day
